title: Old Amira
_note: PRO_03 and after. Lines keep MAIN_QUEST.md IDs where they have one, for voicing. Options show short text; spoken is the fuller line he says. starts: the first whose condition holds opens the conversation.

haddads.speaker: Old Amira
haddads.text: Eleven loaves for the road, and I'm giving the twelfth to the child. Don't argue. Have you heard about the Haddads?

gossip.speaker: Old Amira
gossip.text: [She beams.] Of course you don't. Gone in the night, the Haddads. Took nothing. Not a pot.

gone.speaker: Old Amira
gone.text: Gone in the night. Took nothing. The soldiers say they ran from a debt. Hamza Haddad never owed a copper in his life.

tarik.speaker: Old Amira
tarik.text: [She lowers her voice.] The collector. Tarik. He said it before anyone knew they were gone. Stood at Dalia's stall and said it, bold as you like.

burned.speaker: Old Amira
burned.text: Oh, love. Oh, look at you. Sit. No, sit. There's bread. There's always bread. I can't do anything else, so there's bread.

a13.speaker: Old Amira
a13.text: Tarik? He's not been in the village since. Rides the east road past the crossroads with his riders, every day, drinks at the Haddad gate like he owns it. Maybe he does now.

choices.text: Let me see what you have.

tarikDone.speaker: Old Amira
tarikDone.text: They're saying a ghost took the Collector on the east road. A ghost. [She puts a loaf in your hands and does not look at you.] I left one at Zeyna's door for you too.

idle.speaker: Old Amira
idle.text: Bread, love? Rolls? Something for the little one? [She remembers, sometimes, and stops.]

choices.text: Let me see what you have.
